exact_variant: MOSS-VoiceGenerator, MossTTSDelay architecture. The official card labels it 1.7B. It is distinct from flagship MOSS-TTS (8B Delay / 1.7B Local), which is documented principally for reference-audio cloning.
parameter_count: Official card says 1.7B; Hugging Face API reports exactly 2,114,118,656 BF16 parameters. Counting scope is unspecified, so the sources conflict; methodology not published/found.
reported_weight_size: Hugging Face file metadata reports model.safetensors at exactly 4,228,278,872 bytes. Hub repo usedStorage is 4,239,701,563 bytes (whole repository, not weights alone).
text_description_voice_design: Yes: MOSS-VoiceGenerator accepts text to synthesize plus a free-form natural-language voice/style instruction and explicitly does not require reference audio. This is the MOSS-TTS family component matching text-only custom voice design.
reference_audio_cloning: Separate capability: flagship MOSS-TTS supports zero-shot voice cloning from reference audio; Nano's main documented workflow also supplies prompt audio. Neither is text-only voice design. MOSS-VoiceGenerator is the separate no-reference design model.
language_and_control_coverage: MOSS-VoiceGenerator card specifies Chinese and English. Text instructions can describe voice characteristics, emotion, speed and pitch; examples include age, role, accent and delivery. No broader language coverage found for this exact variant. Paper notes weaker prosody in some English styles and occasional output instability.
code_license: Apache License 2.0, as stated by the official GitHub LICENSE.
weights_license: Hugging Face checkpoint card metadata declares apache-2.0; family repository says family models are Apache-2.0. No separate alternative weights-only license found. Review notices and third-party/data terms before redistribution or production use.
cpu_memory_and_runtime_evidence: Official code selects CPU if CUDA is unavailable, float32 dtype, eager attention: CPU path exists, but no measured CPU speed, peak RAM, minimum RAM or CPU benchmark found. At the API-reported parameter count, FP32 parameter payload alone is 8,456,474,624 bytes by arithmetic; this excludes tokenizer/runtime/overhead and is not measured peak RAM. Card recommends Python 3.12 and Transformers 5.0.0; project gives Debian/Ubuntu setup and a CPU PyTorch backend option, but no formal OS support matrix. GPU/FlashAttention are acceleration options, not shown as mandatory. Published evidence cannot confirm real-time performance or peak RAM on 8 cores/23 GiB.
quality_ranking_evidence: No comparable public TTS Arena/Speech Arena Elo rank or score found: no comparable public rank found. The team's paper (arXiv v1 submitted 2026-03-30) reports InstructTTSEval instruction-following accuracy, not overall quality/MOS: MOSS EN APS/DSD/RP 68.2/82.0/68.7%; ZH 78.0/80.0/74.0%. Qwen3-TTS-VD: EN 78.4/78.8/72.0%, ZH 84.3/82.9/77.4%; Gemini-TTS-Pro: EN 87.6/86.0/67.2%, ZH 89.0/90.1/75.5%. Benchmark covers 6,000 cases, 3 tasks x 2 languages. These percentages are instruction-following, not a single quality ranking. The paper also claims blind pairwise listening wins over Qwen3-TTS-VD, MiniMax Voice Design and MiMo-Audio-7B-Instruct, but exact win percentages were not available in extracted text. Paper methods say 100 pairs, while the model card says 160 internal samples.
github_popularity_evidence: Popularity only, not quality: GitHub API snapshot retrieved 2026-10-10 reports 4,120 stars and 373 forks; Hugging Face model API reports 27,029 downloads and 50 likes. Counts change over time.
integration_notes: Local Python Transformers AutoProcessor/AutoModel example; trust_remote_code=True; accepts text+instruction and writes WAV. Repository includes a Gradio demo script. No stable local REST API/CLI contract for this exact model found. CPU inference path is documented; setup examples also show CUDA wheels, while root docs note selecting the CPU backend.
caveats: Selected MOSS-VoiceGenerator because ordinary MOSS-TTS is documented primarily for reference-audio cloning, not text-description-only voice design.
The 1.7B published label conflicts with Hub API's exact 2,114,118,656 parameter count; sources do not explain why.
MOSS-TTS-Nano is 0.1B and claims CPU streaming on four cores, but its documented workflow is reference-audio cloning; it is not a substitute for the requested text-only voice design.
No measured CPU speed or memory footprint for MOSS-VoiceGenerator. CPU code fallback does not establish usable latency on the provided computer.

The InstructTTSEval scores come from the model team's paper and measure instruction-following, not holistic audio quality. Internal human preference results lack extracted exact percentages and are not a public leaderboard rank.
The card recommends Python 3.12, matching the provided 3.12.3. No install or download was performed. State checked through 2026-10-10.
